text:
samir: seeing a burst of apiserver 502/504s in eu-west3 right now, started ~8m ago. Not full outage but many client retries.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] apiserver 5xx burst detected (eu-west3) - rolling 5m error rate x6.

samir: logs show a lot of proxy dial errors and watch backlog growth:
```
E1202 11:32:10.112 apiserver.go:312] proxy error: dial tcp 10.64.2.9:6443: connect: connection reset by peer
E1202 11:32:10.210 apiserver.go:330] watch queue length: 5090
```

ivy: digging infra metrics 11:31: NAT ephemeral port usage jumped from ~40% -> 97% within 2m, but unusual pattern: egress path flipped between two upstream peering routers due to a BGP route change.

nate: confirmed: cloud provider had a transient peering flap in the region at 11:30 that moved customer NAT egress to a different edge with a smaller ephemeral pool. Combined with a GPU onboarding wave, we exhausted ports.

ops-bot: [AUTOMATION] Detected high conntrack and ephemeral usage; recommending port-preserving SNAT and spinning additional NATs.

marco: autoscaler kicked off ~150 preemptible GPU attaches at 11:28 (image pulls + kubelet heartbeats). Sidecars for our monitoring agent also open long-lived outbound sockets to central telemetry which exacerbates ephemeral usage.

samir: interesting 1 - the monitoring sidecar was recently updated in the GPU image to use an agent that polls often. Could be multiplying connections.

ivy: quick mitigation I can run: 1) enable port-preserving SNAT at the edge, 2) add a spare NAT gateway and redistribute control-plane egress, 3) temporarily reduce autoscaler attach concurrency. Which should we do first?

nate: do port-preserving SNAT first (cheap, fast), then add NAT if still high. I'll also ask networking to pin control-plane egress to the more stable peering path.

marco: i'll patch the autoscaler canary to max_parallel_attach=3 and add a 45s backoff. Small canary to 5% nodepool now.

ops-bot: helm canary scheduled: gpu-autoscaler v3.7.0-canary at 12:00 UTC (staggered attach).

samir: also, controller-manager showing increased lease renew failures during the spike. Suggest bumping leaseDuration/renewDeadline by 50% as a stopgap.

ivy: raised INFRA-8345 to track port-preserve, NAT add, and sidecar change. attaching BGP event logs and conntrack dumps. :spiral_note_pad:

finance-bot: [INFO] Estimated incremental cost for extra NAT in eu-west3 = $195/day.

marco: we should consider changing the monitoring agent to aggregate via a local relay to reduce outbound sockets during onboarding. That'd be a code change but reduces pressure.

nate: network team suggests a medium-term plan: reserve a dedicated small NAT pool for control-plane egress (so customer onboarding can't starve control-plane), and request provider increase ephemeral port range on the stable peering.

samir: agreed. action items: ivy enable port-preserve SNAT now; nate request provider peering pin; marco canary autoscaler + follow up on sidecar; ops-bot create watcher alerts for BGP flaps affecting NAT.

ivy: port-preserve enabled, monitoring shows ephemeral usage dropping to 65% within 90s and apiserver 5xxs falling. watch backlog down to ~700.

samir: great. please keep INFRA-8345 updated with any postmortem notes. we'll include a cost/reliability proposal for reserving control-plane NAT capacity.

marco: filing a small PR to change the monitoring agent to use a relay; will include a rollout plan and canary.

ops-bot: [ACTION] Alerts created: nat_ephemeral_usage > 85% for 1m, apiserver_watch_backlog > 1500 for 2m, etcd_commit_latency > 120ms for 1m.

samir: thanks team. next steps: follow the INFRA ticket, run the autoscaler canary tonight, and finance will model dedicated NAT vs scale-on-demand. Tag me on updates.

finance-bot: CM-4250 created to model tradeoffs (assign finance & infra).

samir: closing thread for now; will reopen if errors recur.
